answer: Within these records, the current meeting time is Thursday at 10:00 local time. The original v1 draft scheduled Thursday at 09:30 local time; the later signed v2 amendment moves it to 10:00 and expressly says it replaces v1’s time. This conclusion is limited to the supplied records.

approaches.description: Read v1 as the original schedule and v2 as the later replacement instruction, then apply v2's explicit replacement statement.
approaches.reason: The amendment directly identifies the v1 time as replaced.

claims.basis_reference: schedule-original states the v1 draft time.
claims.statement: The supplied v1 draft schedules the project review for Thursday at 09:30 local time.

claims.basis_reference: schedule-amendment states the v2 time and that it replaces v1's time.

citations.quote: project review moved to Thursday at 10:00 local time.
This amendment replaces the time in v1.

claims.statement: The supplied signed v2 amendment moves the project review to Thursday at 10:00 local time and says it replaces the v1 time.

claims.basis_reference: Derived in step-current-time from the amendment's stated replacement of v1.
claims.statement: Within the supplied records, Thursday at 10:00 local time is the current supported meeting time; Thursday at 09:30 local time is the original schedule only.

proof_steps.justification: The later supplied record explicitly says that its 10:00 time replaces the time in v1. Therefore, when distinguishing the original schedule from the current instruction within these records, retain 09:30 as historical and use 10:00 as current.
proof_steps.statement: Apply the v2 amendment's explicit replacement statement to the v1 draft time.
